literal_edits.after: 1.1 Put $L=|\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma|$ and let $E=\{rq:0\le r<1,\ q\in L\}$ inside the Euclidean coordinate space on the vertices of the link, with the subspace topology. For an empty link both the cone by convention and $E=\{0\}$ are a single apex, so assume $L\ne\varnothing$. The continuous map $L\times[0,1)\to E$, $(q,r)\mapsto rq$, identifies exactly $L\times\{0\}$ with the apex: if $rq=r'q'$ with $r,r'>0$, coordinate sums give $r=r'$ and then $q=q'$. It therefore descends to a continuous bijection $\varphi:c_{<1}(L)\to E$. For each $0<t<1$, the closed radial cone $(L\times[0,t])/(L\times\{0\})$ is compact by [F2], and its continuous bijection onto $E_t=\{rq:0\le r\le t,\ q\in L\}$ is a homeomorphism because $E_t$ is Hausdorff. Away from the apex the inverse on the full open cone is continuous by $r=\sum_vz_v$, $q=z/r$, followed by the quotient projection. At the apex, the preimage of any quotient-open neighbourhood is an open set containing $L\times\{0\}$. Product neighbourhoods of its points, a finite cover of the compact link $L$, and the minimum of their positive radii give an $\epsilon>0$ with $L\times[0,\epsilon)$ in that preimage. The relatively open set $\{z\in E:\sum_vz_v<\epsilon\}$ is consequently mapped by $\varphi^{-1}$ into the given neighbourhood. Thus the inverse is continuous at the apex too, and $\varphi$ is a homeomorphism of the full open cone. [F1, F2, construct]

historical_prototype_Proof1_1: Represent the cone in the Euclidean coordinate space on the link vertices as $E=\{rq:0<r<1,\ q\in|\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma|\}\cup\{0\}$. The quotient map sends $(q,r)$ to $rq$. It is a continuous bijection after collapsing the zero end. Away from zero its inverse is $r=\sum_vz_v$, $q=z/r$. At zero, any quotient-open neighborhood contains $|\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma|\times[0,\epsilon)$ for some $\epsilon>0$: for each link point choose a product neighborhood about $(q,0)$, take a finite cover of the compact link, and take the smallest positive radius. Thus the bijection and its inverse are continuous at zero too. For an empty link use $E=\{0\}$. [F1, F2, construct]
